title: Drip cake decoration
subtitle: controlled chocolate or ganache drips down the sides of a buttercream cake
excerpt: Drip decoration sends a thin stream of chocolate ganache down the sides of a chilled, frosted cake to create a clean cascade effect. The technique takes about fifteen minutes and relies on two things: ganache at the right temperature, and a cake cold enough to set each drip as it runs down the side.
sourceNotes: Drip cake technique popularised in home baking from approximately 2015. Standard ganache ratios and temperature guidance from professional patisserie practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth mixture of chocolate and warm double cream used for glazing, filling, and decoration. For drip cakes, the ratio is usually 2 parts chocolate to 1 part cream by weight.

content.text: sent down the sides of a frosted cake in controlled drops. Done right, each drip runs to a different depth and sets cleanly against the cold buttercream. The ganache temperature is the single variable that matters most: too warm and it runs straight to the board; too cool and it sets before it moves.

Use 2 parts dark chocolate to 1 part double cream by weight. Bring the cream to just below boiling, pour it over finely chopped chocolate, wait two minutes, then stir from the centre out until smooth. Let it cool to 30 to 32°C before using it on the cake. At that temperature, a spoonful dropped on the back of a cold spoon should drip slowly and set within 20 seconds.
The cake must be fully frosted and very cold before dripping begins. Chill it in the fridge for at least 30 minutes after the final coat of buttercream. The cold surface sets each drip as it lands.

Place a cold spoon in the fridge for five minutes. Drip a small amount of ganache onto the back of the cold spoon and observe how it moves. It should flow slowly and begin to set within 20 seconds. If it runs off the spoon and stays liquid, it is too warm. If it barely moves, rewarm it briefly over a bowl of hot water.

Pour the ganache into a squeeze bottle or use a teaspoon. Work around the top edge of the cake, placing small amounts of ganache at intervals of about 3 cm and letting each one run over the edge and down the side. Vary the amount at each point to vary the drip length.
Once the drips are set, pour the remaining ganache onto the top of the cake and spread it to the edge with a palette knife, letting it meet the tops of the drips.
Return the cake to the fridge for 10 minutes for the top layer to set before adding any further decoration.

attrs.problem: Drips running all the way to the board
attrs.avoid: Avoid applying ganache that is still too warm; test it on a cold spoon first.
attrs.fix: Let the ganache cool by a further 2 to 3°C and test again before continuing.

attrs.problem: Drips setting immediately with no flow
attrs.avoid: Avoid starting with ganache below 28°C; it will set on contact before forming a drip.
attrs.fix: Warm the ganache briefly in short bursts over a bowl of hot water, stirring between each, until it just barely flows.
